column3: Contrasts seeking honor through others with all honor belonging to Allah.
Directs believers to seek help through patience and prayer, shaping faithful reliance.
Joins Allah's strength and severe punishment to the fate of those who rejected signs.
States that all honor belongs to Allah and pairs it with severe punishment for evil plotting.
Affirms life for those killed in Allah's path, not the rival-love or power theme.
Names the teacher as one of intense powers, supporting the force vocabulary only.
Explicitly describes making rivals for Allah and regret when punishment is seen.
Tests and patience prepare the believer but do not explain rivals or divine power.
Shows intense love of worldly good, clarifying how love can be wrongly directed.
States that all command belongs to Allah, reinforcing exclusive divine sovereignty.
Confesses belonging and return to Allah, a nearby posture of faith.
Affirms Allah gathers people for the promised Day, only indirectly related to the warning.
Depicts wrongdoers unable to ransom themselves from punishment, extending the final warning.
Gives mercy and guidance to the patient, with no direct rival or power connection.
Allah knows hidden and open things and does not love the proud; tangential corrective.
Compares hostility and affection among groups, not the love of Allah and rivals.
Identifies sacred rites of Allah, but adds little to the verse's argument.
Condemns making rivals for the Creator, directly defining the offense in 2:165.
Warns of a trial reaching wrongdoers and Allah's severe punishment.
Warns against hiding guidance, but does not address rival devotion.
States that rivals are made for Allah to turn people from His way, with a final destination in fire.
Exposes the inability of those called besides Allah, grounding the futility of rivals.
Repentance and clarification show a way back, but are not central to the verse.
Contrasts claimed personal possession with Allah's destruction of those stronger in power.
Forbids taking disbelievers as allies over believers, a related warning against misplaced allegiance.
Links persistent disbelief to an enduring curse, complementing the consequence for wrongdoers.
Affirms that earlier peoples were stronger yet Allah cannot be escaped, clarifying His absolute power.
Calls taking Satan as a protector besides Allah manifest loss, paralleling rival attachment.
Continued punishment without relief extends the severity of the warning.
Allah suffices believers and is strong, mighty, modeling reliance on Him alone.
Shows wrongdoers facing punishment and pleading too late, echoing 2:165's future sight.
The immediate preceding ayah declares one God with no god besides Him, the basis for rejecting rivals.
Mentions a loved victory from Allah, offering a lawful object of hope rather than rival love.
Describes one who calls Allah in distress then makes rivals for Him, directly illustrating the pattern.
The immediate preceding signs of creation supply the rational evidence against assigning rivals.
Mentions producing grain only; no meaningful contribution to 2:165.
Shows attachment to false gods and the later sight of punishment.
Contrasts gratitude with disbelief and warns of Allah's severe punishment.
Names excessive love of wealth, illustrating disordered love without rival worship.
Creation and Allah's power to gather support His power, but only broadly.
Contrasts fearing people like or more than Allah, illuminating misdirected fear and devotion.
Explicitly says there is no power except through Allah, reinforcing that power belongs to Him.
Links rejection of Allah's signs to His being strong and severe in punishment.
Criticizes love of the immediate world while neglecting a weighty Day, a parallel to misplaced love.
Contrasts severe punishment for disbelief with forgiveness and reward for believers.
Declares that Allah was not appraised as He deserves and affirms His strength and might.
Discusses reluctant spending and hostility, without clarifying 2:165's core.
Calls a hired worker strong and trustworthy; human strength is not the verse's point.
Shows Allah saving believers and seizing wrongdoers, reinforcing the warning to oppressors.
Names Allah as the strong, mighty provider, supporting exclusive divine power.
Describes apparent collective force with divided hearts; only a loose contrast to all power being Allah's.
Affirms Allah is strong and mighty while speaking of support for Him and His messengers.
The same surah forbids making rivals for Allah after recalling His provision and creation.
Places Allah's forgiveness and mercy above what people gather, only indirectly correcting attachments.
Explicitly names Allah as the provider and possessor of firm power.
Describes Allah's painful, severe seizure of wrongdoing towns, clarifying severe punishment.
Warns Qarun not to exult and notes Allah does not love the exultant, tangential to rival love.
All that is in the heavens and earth is subjected from Allah, supporting His comprehensive dominion.
Calls for worshiping only Allah and not taking one another as lords besides Him.
Affirms life, death, and gathering by Allah, broadly supporting final accountability.
Commands obedience to the messenger by Allah's permission and presents repentance.
Fire as reminder and provision for travelers adds no clear connection.
Mentions bringing forth grain and vegetation only.
Forbids taking even fathers and brothers as allies when they prefer disbelief, sharpening loyalty boundaries.
Creation and vegetation are signs for believers, broadly resonating with Allah's signs.
Promise to fill Hell with followers of Satan relates only generally to consequences.
Allah saves believers and is the strong, mighty one, supporting His power in judgment.
Prohibits excess in eating and drinking, without bearing on rival love.
Wrongdoers behold their Lord and receive punishment for disbelief, echoing future exposure.
Reports preferential human love within a family, not devotion toward rivals.
States that one's striving will be seen; no clear contribution.
Criticizes love of the immediate world, a concise parallel to misplaced love.
Depicts criminals seeing angels without good news, an indirect judgment scene.
Makes the hereafter's punishment a sign and gathers people for a witnessed Day.
Questions claimed knowledge of the unseen, without a close thematic link.
Allah creates all on earth and orders the heavens, supporting His exclusive creatorship.
Affirms Allah sees, which adds only general accountability.
Contrasts believers' recompense with Allah's lack of love for disbelievers.
Hell being displayed to the seer is a remote echo of seeing punishment.
Makes love of Allah operative through following the messenger, clarifying true love for Allah.
Reviving dead earth and producing grain are signs, but contribute little beyond 2:164.
Gives severe punishment to those who dispute concerning Allah, supporting the threat.
Describes paradise shade and climate, unrelated to the ayah's central themes.
Forbids aggression because Allah does not love aggressors; only a shared love term.
Questions disputing what is seen, without relevant content.
A jinn claims strength and trustworthiness; not divine power or rival devotion.
Equates people's trial with Allah's punishment, revealing a false comparison between creatures and Allah.
Allah does not love persistent sinful disbelievers; a general moral contrast.
Condemns religious leaders' corruption and hoarding, with no direct rival-love link.
Denies humans any power or helper, underscoring creaturely helplessness.
Declares all dominion belongs to Allah on that Day, reinforcing His final authority.
Allah will surely question them all, adding general accountability.
Resurrection and creation signs support judgment, but not the verse's rival-love argument.
Opening a gate of severe punishment leaves them despairing, extending the punishment motif.
Rewards obedience to Allah and the messenger, but does not address rivals or power.
Selects the most defiant faction against the Merciful, a remote judgment connection.
Contrasts guidance for believers with deafness and blindness for unbelievers.
The sun and moon being joined is an end-time sign with little explanatory value.
People stand before the Lord of the worlds, supporting accountability only.
Warns those preferring comfort over striving that Hell's heat is more severe.
Denies any protector or helper besides Allah, excluding alternate reliance.
Names Allah as the protector of believers, framing proper allegiance.
Testifies that there is no god but Allah, establishing the denial of rivals.
Forbids taking angels and prophets as lords, a direct boundary against rival lordship.
Declares associating partners with Allah an immense wrong that is not forgiven.
Repeats that associating partners with Allah is an enormous straying.
Describes calling upon beings besides Allah, exposing the object of false devotion.
Challenges worship of what cannot harm or benefit apart from Allah.
Rejects calling upon what neither benefits nor harms besides Allah.
Describes making the jinn partners for Allah despite His creating them.
Explicitly commands that nothing be associated with Allah.
Forbids associating with Allah that for which He sent down no authority.
Questions associating beings that create nothing and are themselves created.
Calls those invoked besides Allah servants like their callers, denying their divinity.
Describes taking religious authorities and the Messiah as lords besides Allah.
Denies any protector or helper besides Allah, reinforcing exclusive dependence.
Describes worshiping what neither harms nor benefits besides Allah and claiming intercession.
Questions the supposed partners invoked besides Allah as mere conjecture.
Contrasts many lords with Allah, the One, the Subduer.
States that judgment belongs only to Allah and commands worship of Him alone.
Contrasts Allah's true call with the unanswered calls made besides Him.
Challenges taking protectors besides Allah who possess neither benefit nor harm.
Asks whether partners have been assigned to Allah and exposes false naming.
Asks whether the Creator can be equated with one who creates nothing.
States that those called besides Allah create nothing and are themselves created.
Forbids taking two gods and declares that He alone is God.
Describes worshiping besides Allah what owns no provision or power.
Shows associators confronting their alleged partners and disowning their own association.
Forbids placing another god with Allah, with disgrace and abandonment as consequence.
Denies that those called besides Allah can remove or shift harm.
Rejects taking gods besides Allah without clear authority.
Describes taking gods besides Allah in pursuit of honor, directly correcting false sources of honor.
States that alleged gods will reject their worship and become opponents.
Identifies Allah alone as God, whose knowledge encompasses all things.
Argues that multiple gods in heaven and earth would have corrupted both.
Challenges taking gods besides Allah and demands proof for the claim.
Challenges worshiping besides Allah what neither benefits nor harms.
Describes calling besides Allah what neither harms nor benefits as far straying.
Portrays calling one whose harm is nearer than benefit, exposing false protection.
Describes worshiping besides Allah that for which no authority or knowledge exists.
Denies any god alongside Allah and argues that rival gods would contend for dominion.
Warns against calling another god with Allah without proof and links it to failure.
Describes taking gods besides Allah that create nothing and lack control over life and death.
Identifies taking one's desire as a god, directly expanding the meaning of rival devotion.
Forbids calling another god with Allah under threat of punishment.
Questions whether any god is with Allah after His acts of creation and provision.
Depicts Allah asking where the alleged partners are on the Day of judgment.
Challenges the alleged partners to respond when they are called.
Forbids calling another god with Allah and affirms that all judgment belongs to Him.
Describes worshiping idols besides Allah and affirms provision comes from Allah alone.
Compares protectors taken besides Allah to the frailest of houses.
Rejects sharing Allah's provision with equals, using a human analogy against partners.
Names association with Allah as a tremendous wrong.
Denies that those called besides Allah own even the weight of an atom or share in dominion.
States that those called besides Allah do not possess even a date-stone's thin membrane.
Rejects taking gods besides Allah that cannot avert harm or save.
Describes taking gods besides Allah in hope of help, exposing false expectation.
Records taking protectors besides Allah to draw near, then assigns judgment to Allah.
Challenges reliance on those called besides Allah when Allah intends harm or mercy.
Questions taking intercessors besides Allah even when they possess nothing and do not understand.
Assigns all intercession to Allah and affirms His dominion.
Contrasts aversion at Allah being mentioned alone with delight in those besides Him.
Identifies rejection when Allah alone is called and belief when partners are associated.
Contrasts Allah's judgment with those called besides Him, who judge nothing.
Rejects being called to associate with Allah what lacks knowledge and calls instead to the Mighty Forgiver.
Commands devotion to the one God, directly opposing association.
Questions taking protectors besides Allah and identifies Allah as the true protector.
Questions whether partners have authorized a religion Allah did not permit.
Challenges alleged partners to show what they created or their share in the heavens.
Calls most astray those who invoke besides Allah what will not answer until the Day of judgment.
States that the invoked will become enemies and deny their worship.
Names the revered idols, setting up their exposure as unsupported objects of devotion.
Denies authority for the named objects of worship and identifies them as conjectural names.
Forbids calling anyone alongside Allah in places of worship.
Declares calling only upon the Lord and associating no one with Him.
